title: When one job is no longer the plan
text: {{1}} a growing number of workers, the question 'What do you do?' needs a list rather than a single answer. The portfolio career — a blend {{2}} part-time employment, freelancing, tutoring and a small business on the side — used to be a rarity, but digital platforms {{3}} made {{4}} easier than ever {{5}} assemble a living from several sources at once. Supporters point out that no single employer can sink them and that varied work keeps their skills fresh. Sceptics reply {{6}} pensions and sick pay matter, that such arrangements offer {{7}} security, not more, and that a portfolio often means working evenings to keep the plates spinning. The open question is {{8}} the portfolio life offers freedom or simply insecurity with better branding.

gaps.explanation: 'For someone' — from their point of view.
Present perfect with a plural subject: have made.
'Make it easier to…' — the dummy object before the infinitive.
The infinitive completes 'made it easier to assemble'.
Uncountable 'security' with the contrast 'not more': less security.
